<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Market Risks</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are exposed to various market risks, including changes in commodity prices and changes in interest rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commodity Price Risks</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the ordinary course of business, we may enter into various types of transactions involving financial instruments to manage and reduce the impact of changes in commodity prices, including price risk on anticipated purchases of corn, natural gas and the sale of ethanol. We do not enter into derivatives or other financial instruments for trading or speculative purposes.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">62<a name="PB_62_072030_8146"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='62',FILE='C:\JMS\106319\11-31380-1\task5170440\31380-1-bo.htm',USER='106319',CD='Mar  8 02:24 2012' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are subject to market risk with respect to the price and availability of corn, the principal raw material we use to produce ethanol and ethanol by-products. In general, rising corn prices result in lower profit margins and, therefore, represent unfavorable market conditions. This is especially true when market conditions do not allow us to pass along increased corn costs to our customers. The availability and price of corn is subject to wide fluctuations due to unpredictable factors such as weather conditions, farmer planting decisions, governmental policies with respect to agriculture and international trade, and global demand and supply. Our weighted-average gross corn cost for the year ended December 31, 2011, was approximately 96.1% higher than for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160; Our weighted-average gross corn cost for the year ended December 31, 2010, was approximately 5.3% higher than for the year ended December 31, 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have firm-price purchase commitments with some of our corn suppliers under which we agree to buy corn at a price set in advance of the actual delivery of that corn. Under these arrangements, we assume the risk of a decrease in the market price of corn between the time this price is fixed and the time the corn is delivered.&#160; At December 31, 2011, we had firm-price purchase commitments to purchase approximately 1.2 million bushels of corn for delivery through February 2012.&#160; We also had future contracts to sell 45 thousand bushels of corn.&#160; At December 31, 2010, we had firm-price purchase commitments to purchase approximately 3.0 million bushels of corn for delivery through March 2011.&#160; We have elected to account for these transactions as normal purchases under ASC 815, and accordingly, did not mark these transactions to market.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, we enter into commodity futures contracts in connection with the purchase of corn to reduce our risk of future price increases. We account for these transactions under ASC 815. These futures contracts are not designated as hedges and, therefore, are marked to market each period, with corresponding gains and losses recorded in &#147;(Loss) gain on derivative transactions, net&#148; on the condensed consolidated statements of operations. The fair value of these derivative contracts is recognized in other current assets in the condensed consolidated balance sheet, net of any cash received from the brokers. At December 31, 2011, we had 9 short March 2012 corn future contracts at an average price of $6.34 per bushel.&#160; At December 31, 2010, we had 765 long March 2011 corn futures contracts at an average price of $6.01 per bushel.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are also subject to market risk with respect to ethanol pricing. Our ethanol sales are priced using contracts that can either be based upon a fixed price or based upon a market price at the time of shipment. We sometimes fix the price at which we sell ethanol using fixed price physical delivery contracts. At December 31, 2011, we had contracts to sell 3.9 million gallons of ethanol at fixed prices.&#160; At December 31, 2010, we had fixed price contracts to sell 11.7 million gallons of ethanol.&#160; These sale transactions would not be marked to market as they qualify for the normal sales exemption under ASC 815.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, we also sell forward ethanol using contracts where the price is determined at a point in the future based upon an ethanol index price plus or minus a fixed amount. At December 31, 2011, we had sold 58.1 million gallons of ethanol at index prices using Platts and OPIS indices. At December 31, 2010, we had sold 17.6 million gallons of ethanol at index prices using Platts and OPIS indices. When we have these arrangements, we assume the risk of a price decrease in the market price of ethanol.&#160; These sale transactions would not be marked to market as they qualify for the normal sales exemption under ASC 815.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, we enter into ethanol futures contracts and ethanol swaps contracts in connection with the sale of ethanol. We account for these transactions under ASC 815. These futures contracts are not designated as hedges and, therefore, are marked to market each period, with corresponding gains and losses recorded in &#147;(Loss) gain on derivative transactions, net&#148; on the condensed consolidated statements of operations. The fair value of these derivative contracts is recognized in prepaid expenses and other current assets in the condensed consolidated balance sheet, net of any cash received from the brokers. At December 31, 2011, we were long 210 thousand gallons of Platts&#146; swaps.&#160; For the Platts&#146; swaps, 3.1 million were</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">63<a name="PB_63_072135_7091"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">expired but still subject to settlement.&#160; We did not have any futures contracts to sell ethanol at December 31, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We may also be subject to market risk with respect to our supply of natural gas which is consumed during the production of ethanol and its co-products and has historically been subject to volatile market conditions. Natural gas prices and availability are affected by weather conditions, overall economic conditions and foreign and domestic governmental regulation.&nbsp; At December 31, 2011, we had purchased forward 527,000 MMBtu&#146;s of natural gas at an average fixed price of $3.28 per MMBtu through January 2012.&#160; At December 31, 2010, we had purchased forward 477,300 MMBtu&#146;s of natural gas at an average fixed price of $4.30 per MMBtu through the first quarter of 2011. We have elected to account for these transactions as normal purchases under ASC 815 and, accordingly, have not marked these transactions to market.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We prepared a sensitivity analysis to estimate our exposure to market risk of our daily net commodity position. Our daily net commodity position consists of merchandisable agricultural commodity inventories, related purchase and sale contracts, and exchange-traded futures and exchange-traded and over-the-counter option contracts, including those contracts used to hedge portions of production requirements. The fair value of such daily net commodity position is a summation of the fair values calculated for each commodity by valuing each net position at quoted futures prices. Market risk is estimated as the potential loss in fair value resulting from a hypothetical 10% adverse change in such prices. Based on the analysis performed, our highest position through the year ended December 31, 2011, had a fair value of $53.8 million, which would result in a $5.4 million market risk.&nbsp; Our lowest position at December 31, 2011, had a fair value of $88.9 thousand, which would result in an $8.9 thousand market risk.&nbsp; Our average position at December 31, 2011, was approximately $16.5 million, for an average market risk of $1.7 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Interest Rate Risk</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The primary market risk associated with the Term Loan Agreement is sensitivity to changes in the interest rate. Borrowings under the Term Loan Agreement bear interest at (i) LIBOR (2% floor) plus 8.5% per annum or (ii) the alternate base rate plus 7.5% per annum.&#160; The risk management strategies that we employ use various risk sensitivity metrics to measure such risks and to examine behavior under significant adverse market conditions. We performed a sensitivity analysis that measures the change in interest expense on our variable rate debt arising from a hypothetical 100 basis point adverse movement in interest rates. Based on our outstanding variable rate debt as of December 31, 2011, a hypothetical 100 basis point change in interest rates would not impact our interest expense because the adjusted LIBOR rate as of December 31, 2011, was 0.58% compared to our minimum Term Loan Facility adjusted LIBOR rate of 2.00% per annum according to the Term Loan Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Material Limitations</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The disclosures with respect to the above noted risks do not take into account the underlying commitments or anticipated transactions.&#160; If the underlying items were included in the analysis, the gains or losses on the futures contracts may be offset.&#160; Actual results will be determined by a number of factors that are not generally under our control and could vary significantly from those results disclosed.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are exposed to credit losses in the event of nonperformance by counterparties on the above instruments, as well as credit or performance risk with respect to our hedged commitments. Although nonperformance is possible, we do not anticipate nonperformance by any of these parties.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the supervision of, and with the participation of management, including our Chief Executive Officer, John W. Castle, and Chief Financial Officer, Calvin Stewart, the Company carried out an evaluation of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report.&#160; Based upon that evaluation, Mr.&nbsp;Castle and Mr.&nbsp;Stewart have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures have been designed and are effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the rules&nbsp;and forms of the Securities and Exchange Commission.&#160; These disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in such reports is accumulated and communicated to our management, including Mr.&nbsp;Castle and Mr.&nbsp;Stewart, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding the required disclosure.&#160; The design of any system of controls is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events.&#160; There can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goal under all potential future conditions, regardless of how remote.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based upon the evaluation performed by our management, which was conducted with the participation of Mr.&nbsp;Castle and Mr.&nbsp;Stewart, there has been no change in our internal control over financial reporting during the fourth quarter of 2011 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as such term is defined in 13a-15(f)&nbsp;or Rule&nbsp;15d-15(f)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act. &#160;Management, with the participation of Mr.&nbsp;Castle and Mr.&nbsp;Stewart, assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; In making this assessment, management used the framework set forth in <i>Internal Control-Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160; Based upon this assessment, our management concluded that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, our internal control over financial reporting was effective to provide reasonable assurance that the desired control objectives were achieved.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Inherent Limitation of the Effectiveness of Internal Control</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can only provide reasonable, not absolute assurance that the objectives of the internal control system are met.&#160; Because of the inherent limitations of any internal control system, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues, if any, within a company have been detected.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9B.&#160; Other Information</font></b><a name="Item9b_OtherInformation_064844"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Executive Officers</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">John W. Castle. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Castle was appointed Chief Executive Officer on November&nbsp;22, 2011.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Castle has been a Director since August&nbsp;2011.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Castle joined the Company in April&nbsp;2010 as Chief Financial Officer. Before joining the Company, Mr.&nbsp;Castle served as Senior Vice President of Operations and Chief Financial Officer of White Energy,&nbsp;Inc., an ethanol production company, starting in November&nbsp;2005. From August&nbsp;2004 to November&nbsp;2005, Mr.&nbsp;Castle was director of accounting for Dresser,&nbsp;Inc., a global manufacturer of highly engineered energy infrastructure and oilfield products and services. Mr.&nbsp;Castle has also served as Vice President and Chief Financial Officer at Rohn Industries,&nbsp;Inc. and as Vice President, Treasurer and Corporate Controller of Telxon Corporation. Previously, Mr.&nbsp;Castle was a member of Paxton Associates LLC, a provider of financial and operational assessment services. Mr.&nbsp;Castle has also held accounting and financial management positions at Mosler Inc. and Litton Industries,&nbsp;Inc. Mr.&nbsp;Castle is a Certified Public Accountant with a Masters of Business Administration from Xavier University and a Bachelor of Science in Accounting from Eastern Illinois University.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Calvin Stewart. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Stewart was appointed Chief Financial Officer on November&nbsp;22, 2011.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Stewart joined the Company in November&nbsp;2010 as Chief Accounting and Compliance Officer. Prior to joining the Company, Mr.&nbsp;Stewart served most recently as Chief Financial Officer of White Energy,&nbsp;Inc., an ethanol production company. Mr.&nbsp;Stewart joined White Energy in June&nbsp;2006 as Corporate Controller. From August&nbsp;2004 to June&nbsp;2006, Mr.&nbsp;Stewart served as Manager, Technical Accounting and Sr. Manager, Corporate Accounting, at Dresser,&nbsp;Inc., a global manufacturer of highly engineered energy infrastructure and oilfield products and services. Previously, Mr.&nbsp;Stewart was Manager, Accounting and Finance, at Siemens Maintenance Services. Mr.&nbsp;Stewart also served as Plant Operations Controller and Director of Accounting and Finance for Morningstar Foods, a national leader in dairy food and beverage manufacturing and distribution. Mr.&nbsp;Stewart is a Certified Public Accountant with a Masters of Business Administration from Southern Methodist University&#146;s Edwin L. Cox School of Business and a Bachelor of Science in Finance, cum laude, from Towson University.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Benjamin J. Borgen. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Borgen became our Senior Vice President, Commodity Risk Management in March&nbsp;2010. From June&nbsp;2009 to February&nbsp;2010, Mr.&nbsp;Borgen managed ethanol trading as Director of Commodity Trading for Barclays Capital. From April&nbsp;2008 to May&nbsp;2009, Mr.&nbsp;Borgen served as Director of Ethanol Trading at Saracen Energy Partners. Mr.&nbsp;Borgen served as Vice President of Ethanol Trading and Marketing for Sempra Energy Trading, from March&nbsp;2005 to March&nbsp;2008. Mr.&nbsp;Borgen was also a Senior </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under our third amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws, the number of directors at any one time is set by resolution of the Board. Currently, the Board consists of six members, of which three have affirmatively been determined to be independent. Upon emergence from bankruptcy and appointment of our new Board, the Board affirmatively determined that Messrs.&nbsp;Davis, Bernlohr and Cellar are independent of the Company and our management under the NASDAQ Stock Market Rules&nbsp;and Rule&nbsp;10A-3 of the Exchange Act. In addition, although the Board has not made a formal determination on the matter, we believe that Messrs.&nbsp;Hawks and Silverman may not be independent of the Company and our management under the NASDAQ Stock Market Rules. In making this independence determination, we noted in particular the following: (i)&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Hawks is an original partner with Brigade, (ii)&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Silverman is a Managing Partner and Co-Chief Investment Officer with Senator, (iii)&nbsp;Brigade received approximately 27% in aggregate principal amount of Notes and shares of common stock sold in a private placement that closed on March&nbsp;15, 2010, (iv)&nbsp;Senator received approximately 12% in aggregate principal amount of Notes and shares of common stock sold in a private placement that closed on March&nbsp;15, 2010, (v)&nbsp;Senator and Brigade received an aggregate of $500,000 as a commitment fee as consideration for their commitment to backstop our August&nbsp;2010 Notes offering and (vi)&nbsp;Senator and Brigade are lenders under the Term Loan Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We note that The NASDAQ Stock Market LLC does not view ownership of even a significant amount of stock, by itself, as a bar to an independence finding. Although it is unclear under NASDAQ Stock Market Rules&nbsp;whether Messrs.&nbsp;Hawks and Silverman would be considered independent, we do not </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Compensation Committee. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a Compensation Committee that includes Mr.&nbsp;Bernlohr (Chair), Mr.&nbsp;Davis and Mr.&nbsp;Cellar, all of whom are &#145;&#145;independent&#146;&#146; as defined under the federal securities laws. The Compensation Committee administers, subject to Board approval, our stock plans and incentive compensation plans, including our 2010 Equity Incentive Plan. In addition, the Compensation Committee is responsible for making recommendations to the Board with respect to the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and our other executive officers and for making recommendations to the Board with respect to compensation and employee benefit programs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Board has adopted a written charter for the Compensation Committee, which is available on our website at www.aventinerei.com.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Director Nominations. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board has not established a committee responsible for nominating, or<i>  </i>recommending for nomination, directors to our Board. We believe that the entire Board is able to<i>  </i>fulfill the functions of a nominating committee. The Board believes that candidates for director should<i>  </i>have certain minimum qualifications, including being able to read and understand financial statements<i>  </i>and having the highest personal integrity and ethics. The Board will consider such factors as relevant<i>  </i>expertise and experience, ability to devote sufficient time to the affairs of the Company, demonstrated<i>  </i>excellence in his or her field, the ability to exercise sound business judgment and the commitment to<i>  </i>rigorously represent the long-term interests of the Company&#146;s stockholders. Candidates for director are reviewed in the context of the current composition of the Board, the operating requirements of the<i>  </i>Company and the long-term interests of stockholders. The Board currently does not have a formal<i>  </i>process in place for identifying and evaluating nominees for directors. Instead, the Board will use its<i>  </i>network of contacts to identify potential candidates. The Board conducts any appropriate and<i>  </i>necessary inquiries into the backgrounds and qualifications of possible candidates after considering the<i>  </i>function and needs of the Board. The Board has not established procedures for considering nominees<i>  </i>recommended by stockholders. The Board believes that nominees should be considered on a<i>  </i>case-by-case basis on each nominee&#146;s merits, regardless of who recommended such nominee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Board Leadership Structure</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Chairman of the Board sets the agenda for each of our Board meetings and generally presides over the meetings of our Board. However, each of our directors is expected to provide leadership for our Board in the areas where they have particular expertise and each of our Board members from time to time suggests topics for inclusion on the agenda for future Board meetings. We believe that our leadership structure is appropriate because it strikes an effective balance between management and non-employee director participation in the Board process. The role of our Chief Executive Officer, who is also a director, helps to ensure communication between management and the non-employee directors, but also encourages each non-employee director to participate and contribute to the Board process, while also capitalizing on each director&#146;s particular area of expertise as needed. It also increases the non-employee directors&#146; understanding of management decisions and our operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Board Risk Assessment and Control</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our risk management program is overseen by our Board and its committees, with support from our management. Our Board oversees an enterprise-wide approach to ethanol industry risk management, designed to support the achievement of organizational objectives, including strategic objectives, to improve long-term organizational performance and enhance stockholder value. A fundamental part of risk management is a thorough understanding of the risks a company faces, understanding of the level of risk appropriate for the Company and the steps needed to manage those risks effectively. As an example, we may manage commodity price risk by, when appropriate, entering into appropriate hedge agreements with approved counterparties. Our Board takes an active role in determining the types and levels of hedging activity pursued. Together with management&#146;s recommendations, our Board may approve the </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">71<a name="PB_71_064740_141"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">counterparties with whom we enter into hedge agreements and the commodity levels hedged. The involvement of the full Board in setting our business strategy is a key part of its overall responsibilities and together with management determines what constitutes an appropriate level of risk for us.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While the Board has the ultimate oversight responsibility for the risk management process, other committees of the Board also have responsibility for risk management activities. In particular, the Audit Committee focuses on financial risk, including internal controls, and oversees compliance with regulatory requirements. In setting compensation, the Compensation Committee recommends approval of compensation programs for the officers and other key employees to encourage an appropriate level of risk-taking behavior consistent with our business strategy. In determining strategic business decisions, our strategic and finance committee focuses on business and transactional risks.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the fiscal year ended 2011, none of our then executive officers served as a member of the board of directors or Compensation Committee of any entity that had one or more of its executive officers serving as a member of our Board or Compensation Committee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Corporate Governance</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The charters of the Compensation Committee and Audit Committee, as well as our Corporate Governance Guidelines and our Code of Business Conduct and Ethics that applies to our directors, officers and employees (including our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, principal accounting officer, controller or other persons performing similar functions), are available on our website (www.aventinerei.com) or in print upon written request at no charge.&#160; If we amend or grant any waivers under the codes that are applicable to our Chief Executive Officer, our Chief Financial Officer, or our principal accounting officer and that relate to any element of the SEC&#146;s definition of a code of ethics, which we do not anticipate doing, we will promptly post that amendment or waiver on our website, www.aventinerei.com, under &#147;Investor Relations&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 11.&#160; Executive Compensation</font></b><a name="Item11_ExecutiveCompensation_064807"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compensation Program Objectives</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that every decision relating to executive compensation should be made with the aim to enhance stockholder value.&#160; We believe that this overall goal can be achieved by balancing three objectives:</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">72<a name="PB_72_065051_7608"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To reward, and thereby motivate, that talent for sustainable value creation; and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Annual cash bonuses;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity-based awards; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Company-wide benefits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Base Salary. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Base salaries represent the guaranteed portion of total compensation designed to attract and retain managers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Annual Bonuses.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The Company provides a cash bonus opportunity as part of the total expected compensation used to attract and retain its management, as well as a component of rewarding, and thereby encouraging, value creation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2011, the Board approved a bonus plan that provides for awards to senior management based upon achievement of corporate objectives (corporate pool) or commodity risk objectives.&#160; All of the NEOs had half or all of their bonuses funded via the corporate pool of CRM as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Corporate objectives included ramping up of ethanol production across the Company&#146;s plants while controlling production, distribution, and other costs.&#160; The board gauged the degree to which objectives were met using pre-determined guidelines, but ultimately used its judgment in awarding bonuses to managers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Equity-Based Awards. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company grants equity-based compensation as part of the overall expected value of pay used to attract and retain its senior management, as well as a tool for directly aligning the interests of senior managers and the stockholders.&#160; In 2011 certain NEOs were awarded hybrid equity units by the Company.&#160; The assumptions and methodology used to determine such amounts are set forth in Note 19 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Company-wide Benefits.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Senior management does not get any other form of cash or equity compensation or perquisites besides those mentioned in the foregoing description.&#160; Senior management participates in the Company health and retirement programs on the same terms as other employees, whereby contributions made under the plan include a match, at the Company&#146;s discretion, of an employee&#146;s contribution to the plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Summary of Employment Agreements with NEOs</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;19, 2011, the Company announced the retirement of Thomas Manuel as Chief Executive Officer, and the appointment of John Castle as Interim Chief Executive Officer and Calvin Stewart as the Interim Chief Financial Officer.&#160; On November&nbsp;22, 2011, the Company announced the appointment of John Castle as President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors.&#160; The Company also announced the appointment of Calvin Stewart as Chief Financial Officer.&#160; The Company has agreements with all three of the current NEOs, later referred to as the &#147;NEO Employment Agreements.&#148;&#160; Those agreements are summarized as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Employment Agreements</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">John W. Castle. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;21, 2011, the Company and Mr.&nbsp;Castle entered into an employment agreement (the &#145;&#145;Castle Employment Agreement&#146;&#146;) with a term beginning on November&nbsp;1, 2011, and expiring on December&nbsp;31, 2014. The terms of the Castle Employment Agreement provide for, among other things, (i)&nbsp;a base annual salary of $500,000, (ii)&nbsp;an annual bonus with a target of at least 100% of Mr.&nbsp;Castle&#146;s base salary and an opportunity to earn an incentive bonus of up to another 100% of his base salary each year, in each case based on attainment of performance metrics as determined by the Board of Directors or its Compensation Committee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, pursuant to the Castle Employment Agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Castle was awarded options to purchase 100,000 shares of common stock of the Company with an exercise price equal to the per share fair market value of the common stock on May&nbsp;5, 2010, of $43.75, as determined by the Board, and 25,000 shares of Restricted Stock. 50% of the options and 50% of the Restricted Stock will vest in three equal installments on each of the first two anniversaries of May&nbsp;5, 2010, and December&nbsp;31, 2012, subject to Mr.&nbsp;Castle&#146;s continuing employment with the Company. 50% of the options and 50% of the Restricted Stock will vest subject to the attainment of reasonable performance criteria determined by the Board, which were achieved for fiscal year 2010. The options will expire on the 10 year anniversary of May&nbsp;5, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Calvin Stewart.&#160; </font></i><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;22, 2011, the Company and Mr.&nbsp;Stewart entered into an employment agreement (the &#145;&#145;Stewart Employment Agreement&#146;&#146;) with a term beginning on November&nbsp;22, 2011, and expiring on December&nbsp;31, 2014. The terms of the Stewart Employment Agreement provide for, among other things, (i)&nbsp;a base annual salary of $300,000, (ii)&nbsp;an annual bonus with a target of at least 100% of Mr.&nbsp;Stewart&#146;s base salary and an opportunity to earn an incentive bonus of up to another 100% of his base salary each year, in each case based on attainment of performance metrics as determined by the Board of Directors or its Compensation Committee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Benjamin J. Borgen.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;15, 2010, the Company and Mr.&nbsp;Borgen, our Senior Vice President, Commodity Risk Management, entered into an employment agreement (the &#145;&#145;Borgen Employment Agreement&#146;&#146;) with a term expiring on December&nbsp;31, 2012. The terms of the Borgen Employment Agreement provide for, among other things, (i)&nbsp;a base annual salary of $400,000, (ii)&nbsp;an inducement bonus of $120,000, and after 2010, an annual bonus with target of at least 100% of Mr.&nbsp;Borgen&#146;s base salary, and the opportunity to earn an incentive bonus of up to another 100% of his base salary, in each case based on attainment of performance metrics as determined by the Chief Executive Officer of the Company and approved by the Board or the Compensation Committee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, pursuant to the Borgen Employment Agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Borgen was awarded options to purchase 51,300 shares of common stock of the Company with an exercise price at the fair market value on March&nbsp;15, 2010, of $45.60, as determined by the Board, and 55,576 shares of Restricted Stock, under </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">75<a name="PB_75_072147_8627"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Summary of Equity Plans</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">2010 Equity Incentive Plan</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;15, 2010, the Board adopted the Aventine Renewable Energy Holdings,&nbsp;Inc. 2010 Equity Incentive Plan to provide a means through which we can attract and retain key personnel and whereby directors, officers, employees, consultants and advisors (and prospective directors, officers, employees, consultants and advisors) can acquire and maintain an equity interest in us, or be paid incentive compensation, thereby strengthening their commitment to our welfare and aligning their interests with those of our stockholders. The Board or the Compensation Committee will administer the plan, which provides for the following types of awards:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">options to purchase shares of common stock, including both tax-qualified and non-qualified options;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">stock appreciation rights, which provide the participant the right to receive the excess of the fair market value of a specified number of shares of common stock at the time of exercise over the base price of the stock appreciation right, generally payable in shares of common stock;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">stock awards, including grants in the form of (i)&nbsp;shares of common stock that are subject to a restriction period, (ii)&nbsp;rights to receive shares of common stock contingent upon the expiration of a restriction period and (iii)&nbsp;shares of common stock that are not subject to a restriction period or performance measures; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">performance compensation awards, which provide the participant the right, contingent upon the attainment of specified performance measures within a specified period, to receive shares of common stock, or the cash value thereof, if such performance measures are satisfied or met.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employees, directors, consultants, advisors and prospective employees, directors, consultants or advisors of the Company and its affiliates are eligible to receive awards under the 2010 Equity Incentive Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board or a committee of the Board will determine the terms of any awards granted under the 2010 Equity Incentive Plan, including, without limitation, the number of shares subject to an award, vesting criteria, performance conditions, the manner of exercise, and the effect of certain corporate transactions. Unless otherwise provided in an award agreement, awards granted under the plan generally vest, or the restrictions applicable to the awards generally lapse, on the third anniversary of the date of grant. In the event of a &#145;&#145;Change in Control&#146;&#146; (as defined in the plan), the Board or committee may provide for the acceleration of the vesting, lapse of restrictions, or performance periods with respect to all or any portion of outstanding awards. With respect to awards of stock options, unless otherwise provided in an award agreement, unvested options expire upon termination of employment or service of the participant for any reason, and the vested options remain exercisable for (i)&nbsp;one year following termination of employment or service by reason of a participant&#146;s death or disability, but not later than the expiration of the term of the options or (ii)&nbsp;90 days following termination of employment or service for any reason other than the participant&#146;s death or disability, and termination for &#145;&#145;Cause&#146;&#146; (as defined in the plan), but not later than the </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">76<a name="PB_76_072240_7906"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each unit granted for this year will translate into up to one share, depending on the average closing share price for the last 15 trading days of 2014, denoted as &#147;S&#148; in the following formula:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"># Shares = # Units x (1 &#151; 19.6/S)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For example, if a manager is granted 10,000 units, and S equals $40, then the manager would receive 5,100 shares (i.e., 10,000 units x (1 &#151; 19.6/40) = 5,100).&#160; If the stock price ends up higher, then the participant would receive more shares; if the stock price were lower, he or she would receive fewer shares.&#160; If the stock price falls below $19.60, the participant would be granted no shares.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Thomas L. Manuel retired in August&nbsp;2011.&#160; As part of Mr.&nbsp;Manuel&#146;s Mutual release Agreement, the vesting terms of the hybrid equity units were accelerated and vested on the termination date.&#160; We modified the hybrid equity units by changing the measurement date.&#160; The hybrid equity units will now be measured at the average closing share price for the last 15 trading days ending August&nbsp;19, 2012.&#160; This modification did not result in additional compensation expense for the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Retirement Plans; Non-Qualified Deferred Compensation Plans</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other than its 401(k)&nbsp;plan, the Company currently does not maintain any retirement or non-qualified deferred compensation plans for any of its NEOs that provide for the payment of retirement benefits or benefits that will be paid primarily following retirement.&#160; The Company has a 401(k)&nbsp;plan covering substantially all of its employees. Contributions made under the defined contribution plans include a match, at the Company&#146;s discretion, of an employee&#146;s contribution to the plans.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Termination and Change of Control Benefits</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Termination Benefits</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NEO Employment Agreements provide for certain severance benefits upon a termination without &#147;Cause&#148; or for &#147;Good Reason,&#148; which are contingent upon a NEO executing and delivering a general release and waiver of claims in favor of the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The NEO Employment Agreements generally define Cause as:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">willful misconduct or gross negligence of a material nature in the performance of the NEO&#146;s duties;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">being convicted of, or pleading guilty or nolo contendere to a felony (other than a traffic violation);</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">willful theft or embezzlement from the Company or our affiliates; or</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">willful and substantial failure to perform the NEO&#146;s duties or any other material breach of any material provision of the NEO Employment Agreement, which is not cured (if curable) within 30 days following the NEO&#146;s receipt of written notice thereof.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of the NEO Employment Agreements, a NEO has Good Reason to terminate his employment if, without his written consent, any of the following events occurs that are not cured by the Company within 30 days of written notice specifying the occurrence of such Good Reason event, which notice shall be given to the Company within 90 days after the occurrence of the Good Reason event:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a material diminution in authority, duties or responsibilities;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a material diminution in base salary;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a relocation of the NEO&#146;s principal business location to a location outside of Dallas, Texas; or</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">any material breach of the NEO Employment Agreement by the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">John W. Castle.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon termination without Cause or for Good Reason, Mr.&nbsp;Castle is entitled to receive (i)&nbsp;any accrued but unpaid base salary, (ii)&nbsp;any earned but unpaid bonus, (iii)&nbsp;reimbursement for any business expenses, (iv)&nbsp;payment for his accrued but unused vacation, (v)&nbsp;vested accrued benefits to which Mr.&nbsp;Castle is entitled under the Company&#146;s employee benefit plans and programs applicable to Mr.&nbsp;Castle and (vi)&nbsp;subject to Mr.&nbsp;Castle&#146;s signing a general release of claims in the form attached to the Castle Employment Agreement (a)&nbsp;a pro-rata bonus for the year of termination, (b)&nbsp;during the contract term, a lump sum payment equal to the sum of his base salary and bonus and (c)&nbsp;the costs of continued health benefits for a period of 12 months and (vii)&nbsp;immediate vesting and exercisability of any unvested Company equity awards then held by Mr.&nbsp;Castle. The Castle Employment Agreement also restricts Mr.&nbsp;Castle from (i)&nbsp;competing with the Company for 12 months following termination, (ii)&nbsp;soliciting any of the Company&#146;s current employees for 12 months following termination and (iii)&nbsp;disparaging the Company for three years following termination.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Calvin Stewart.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon termination without Cause or for Good Reason, Mr.&nbsp;Stewart is entitled to receive substantially the same benefits as Mr.&nbsp;Castle. The Stewart Employment Agreement also contains restrictions substantially similar to the Castle Employment Agreement.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Benjamin J. Borgen.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon termination without Cause or for Good Reason, Mr.&nbsp;Borgen is entitled to receive substantially the same benefits as Mr.&nbsp;Castle. The Borgen Employment Agreement also contains restrictions substantially similar to the Castle Employment Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Change of Control Benefits</font></i></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The options, Restricted Stock and Restricted Stock Units awarded to each NEO pursuant to their NEO Employment Agreements will vest immediately in the event of a &#147;Change of Control.&#148;&#160; In addition, if (i)&nbsp;any payment or benefit a NEO receives in connection with a Change of Control is subject to the 20% excise tax under Section&nbsp;4999 of the Internal Revenue Code and (ii)&nbsp;the sum of such payments and benefits exceeds 110% of the excise tax threshold, the NEO will be entitled to a gross up payment such the excise tax such that he will be in the same after tax position as if no will be reduced so as not to trigger excise tax under Section&nbsp;4999 of such Code.&#160; If (i) any payment or benefit a NEO receives in connection with a Change of Control is subject to the 20% excise tax under Section&nbsp;4999 of the Internal Revenue Code and (ii) the sum of such payments and benefits does not exceed 110% of the excise tax threshold, the NEO entitlement to the payment and benefits will be reduced in the manner specified in the NEO Employment Agreement, to the level below which no excise tax will be imposed.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For purposes of the NEO Employment Agreements, a Change of Control means the occurrence of any of the following events:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">any person, other than an exempt person (which includes the Company and its subsidiaries and employee benefit plans), becoming a beneficial owner of 50% or more of the shares of common stock or equity interests or voting stock or equity interests of the Company then outstanding;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the consummation of a reorganization, merger or consolidation in which existing Company stockholders or members own less than 50% of the equity of the resulting company;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the consummation of the sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company; or</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">during any 12-month period and provided no other corporation is a majority stockholder of the Company, individuals who on the effective date of our Plan, constitute the Board (the &#145;&#145;Incumbent Board&#146;&#146;) cease for any reason to constitute at least a majority thereof, provided that any person becoming a director subsequent to the effective date of our Plan, whose election or nomination for election was approved by a vote of at least a majority of the directors comprising the Incumbent Board shall be considered a member of the Incumbent Board.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Director Compensation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our compensation program for non-employee directors consists of:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 10.1pt;text-indent:-10.1pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash Compensation</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 10.1pt;text-indent:-10.1pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$50,000 annual cash retainer, payable in equal quarterly installments;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additional $25,000 annual retainer to the Chairman of the Board;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additional committee chair retainers of $10,000 per year for the Chair of the Audit Committee and $5,000 for other Committee Chairs;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1,500 per Board meeting attended ($750 for telephonic meetings); and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$750 per committee meeting attended, either in person or via phone.</font></p>
