<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All fresh start adjustments noted above represent non-recurring fair value measurements and have been treated as non-cash adjustments in the consolidated statement of cash flows.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(13)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Adjustments required in order to report assets and liabilities at fair value under fresh start accounting resulted in a pre-tax charge of $387.7 million, which the Company reported as a loss due to fresh start accounting adjustments in the consolidated statement of operations for the two months ending February&nbsp;28, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the Company eliminated the balance of accumulated other comprehensive gains (net of losses) totaling $2.4 million, which were classified as a loss within reorganization items in the consolidated statement of operations for the two months ending February&nbsp;28, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">3.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The accounting policies below relate to amounts reported in the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Use of Estimates</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. These estimates are based on management&#146;s knowledge of current events and actions that the Company may take in the future. Estimates, by their nature, are based on judgment and available information. Therefore, actual results could differ from those estimates and could have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue is generally recognized when title to products is transferred to an unaffiliated customer as long as the sales price is fixed or determinable and collectability is reasonably assured.&#160; For the majority of sales, this generally occurs after the product has been offloaded at the customers&#146; site.&#160; For others, the transfer of title occurs at the shipment origination point.&#160; The majority of sales are invoiced at the final per unit price which may be a previously contracted fixed price or a market price at the time of shipment.&#160; Other sales are invoiced and the initial receipts are collected based upon a provisional price, and such sales are adjusted to a final price in the same month based upon a monthly-average spot market price.&#160; Sales are made under normal terms and usually do not require collateral.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of sales are based upon freight costs being paid by the Company.&#160; The Company recognizes such freight costs in the financial statements.&#160; In other cases, freight costs are paid by the buyer and the Company excludes these costs from its financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Environmental Expenditures</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Environmental expenditures that pertain to current operations and relate to future revenue are expensed or capitalized consistent with the Company&#146;s capitalization policy.&#160; Expenditures that result from the remediation of an existing condition caused by past operations, and that do not contribute to future revenue, are expensed.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-18<a name="PB_18_103812_563"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Net Income (Loss) Per Share</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with ASC 260, &#147;<i>Earnings Per Share</i>&#148; (&#147;ASC 260&#148;), the Company uses the two-class method to compute basic and diluted earnings per share.&#160; ASC 260 addresses whether instruments granted in share-based payment awards that entitle their holders to receive non-forfeitable dividends or dividend equivalents before vesting should be considered participating securities and need to be included in the earnings allocation in computing net income (loss) per share under the &#147;two-class method.&#148; The two-class method is an earnings allocation formula that determines net income (loss) per share for each class of common stock and participating security according to dividends declared (or accumulated) and participation rights in undistributed earnings. In accordance with the standard, the Company&#146;s restricted stock awards and restricted stock units are considered participating securities because they entitle holders to receive non-forfeitable dividends during the vesting term. In applying the two-class method, undistributed earnings are allocated between common shares, restricted stock awards and restricted stock units.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurement</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for certain financial assets and liabilities under ASC 820, <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures </i>(&#147;ASC 820&#148;).&#160; The Company uses the following methods in estimating fair value disclosures for financial instruments:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash and equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable: </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount reported in the consolidated balance sheets approximates fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revolving credit facility and long-term debt: </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of the Company&#146;s borrowings under its revolving credit facility and the term loan approximates fair value. The fair value of the Notes at December&nbsp;31, 2010, is based upon quoted closing market prices at year-end.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Commodity derivatives: </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commodity derivative instruments, entered into periodically by the Company, consist of futures contracts, swaps and option contracts. The fair value of these commodity derivative instruments are determined by reference to quoted market prices.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Available for sale securities: </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Available for sale securities consists of a common stock investment in an exchange traded security. &#160;The fair value of these securities is determined using quoted market prices.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Note&nbsp;5 for additional information regarding the Company&#146;s fair value assets and liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company considers all highly liquid short-term investments purchased with a maturity of three months or less to be cash equivalents.&#160; Cash equivalents are carried at cost, which approximates fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounts receivable are recorded on a gross basis, with no discounting, less an allowance for doubtful accounts.&#160; Management estimates the allowance for doubtful accounts based on existing economic conditions, the financial conditions of the customers, and the amount and age of past due accounts.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-19<a name="PB_19_103812_9497"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Derivatives and Hedging Activities</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivatives are accounted for in accordance with ASC 815, <i>Derivatives and Hedging</i> (&#147;ASC 815&#148;), and primarily consist of commodity futures contracts, swaps and option contracts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s futures contracts were not designated as hedges and, therefore, are marked to market each period, with corresponding gains and losses recorded in other non-operating income.&#160; Such derivative instruments are recorded at fair value, and are included in &#147;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#148; on the Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheets.&#160; See Note 7.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under ASC 815, companies are required to evaluate contracts to determine whether such contracts are derivatives.&#160; Certain contracts that meet the definition of a derivative under ASC 815 may be exempted from the accounting and reporting requirements of ASC 815 as normal purchases or normal sales. The Company has elected to designate its forward purchases of corn and natural gas and forward sales of ethanol as normal purchases and normal sales under ASC 815.&#160; Accordingly, these contracts are not reflected in the consolidated financial statements until execution.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Property, Plant and Equipment</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Newly acquired land, buildings and equipment are carried at cost less accumulated depreciation.&#160; Depreciation is provided over the estimated useful lives of the assets, generally on the straight-line basis for financial reporting purposes (furniture and fixtures 3 &#151; 20 years, machinery and equipment 5 &#151; 25 years, storage tanks 25 &#151; 30 years, and buildings and improvements 20 &#151; 45 years), and on accelerated methods for tax purposes.&#160; See Note 8.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-lived assets are evaluated for impairment under the provisions of ASC 360, <i>Property, Plant and Equipment</i>.&#160; When facts and circumstances indicate that long-lived assets used in operations may be impaired, and the undiscounted cash flows estimated to be generated from those assets are less than their carrying values, an impairment charge is recorded equal to the excess of the carrying value over fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Cash</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There is no restricted cash at December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; Current restricted cash at December&nbsp;31, 2010, represented cash held to redeem the $155.0 million Notes (see Note 11).&#160; Noncurrent restricted cash represents cash held in segregated bank accounts of the Company, which is set aside as collateral to fund certain letters of credit and utility deposits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Available for sale securities</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Available for sale securities at December&nbsp;31, 2011, consisted of shares of Imperial Petroleum Inc. (&#147;Imperial&#148;).&#160; In December 2011, the Company recognized a non-cash loss on available-for-sale securities of $0.5 million due to the declining market value of the Imperial stock which was determined to be other than temporary.&#160; In October&nbsp;2010, the Company sold all of its available for sale securities consisting of Great Plains Renewable Energy (&#147;GPRE&#148;) stock and recognized a loss of approximately $2.0 million in &#147;Loss on available-for-sale securities&#148; on the consolidated statement of operations for the ten months ended December&nbsp;31, 2010. See Note 6.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Employment-Related Benefits</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employment-related benefits associated with pensions and postretirement health care are expensed as actuarially determined.&#160; The recognition of expense is impacted by estimates made by management, such as discount rates used to value certain liabilities, investment rates of return on plan assets, increases in future wage amounts and future health care costs.&#160; The Company uses third-party specialists to assist management in appropriately measuring the expense and liabilities associated with employment-related benefits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company determines its actuarial assumptions for the pension and post retirement plans, after consultation with its actuaries, on December&nbsp;31 of each year to calculate liability information as of that date and pension and postretirement expense for the following year.&#160; The discount rate assumption is determined based on a spot yield curve that includes bonds that are rated Corporate AA or higher with maturities that match expected benefit payments under the plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets reflects the projected returns for the investment mix and is determined by taking into account the expected weighted averages of the investments of the assets, the fact that the plan assets are actively managed to mitigate downside risks, the historical </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-21<a name="PB_21_103812_5250"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Employee Stock Plans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for its employee stock compensation in accordance with ASC 718, <i>Compensation&nbsp;&#151; Stock Compensation </i>(&#147;ASC 718&#148;).&#160; Stock options are expensed based on their grant date fair value. As required under the guidance, an accounting estimate of the number of shares that are expected to vest is made and then expensed utilizing the grant-date fair value of the shares from the date of grant through the end of the performance cycle period.&#160; See Note 19.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred tax liabilities and assets are recorded for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or tax returns.&#160; Property, plant and equipment, stock-based compensation expense, debt issuance costs and original issue discount are the primary sources of these temporary differences. Deferred income taxes also include net operating loss and capital loss carryforwards.&#160; The Company establishes valuation allowances to reduce deferred tax assets to amounts it believes are realizable.&#160; These valuation allowances and contingency reserves are adjusted based upon changing facts and circumstances. See Note 17.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Concentrations</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Labor Concentration</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Approximately 45% of the Company&#146;s full-time employees at December&nbsp;31, 2011 (comprised of the hourly employees at the Illinois facilities), are covered by a collective bargaining agreement between Aventine&#146;s subsidiary, Aventine Renewable Energy,&nbsp;Inc., and the United Steelworkers International Union, Local 7-662 (the &#147;Union&#148;).&#160;&#160; On October&nbsp;29, 2010, the Union ratified a new collective bargaining agreement with Aventine Renewable Energy,&nbsp;Inc. for its hourly production workers in Pekin,&nbsp;Illinois. This new agreement is effective November&nbsp;1, 2010, and runs through October&nbsp;31, 2012. The agreement contains provisions, terms and conditions that are customary in collective bargaining agreements of this type, including, among other things, wages, hours, work assignments, management rights, seniority, arbitration and grievance procedures, benefits, vacations and holidays. The benefit and base wage packages for the currently covered employees remain substantially similar to those in the previous collective bargaining agreement; the currently covered employees received lump sum annual payments of $750 in November&nbsp;2010 and November&nbsp;2011. Employees hired after November&nbsp;1, 2010, will only be eligible for the 401(k)&nbsp;program as their retirement benefit. The collective bargaining agreement may not prevent a strike or work stoppage&nbsp;in the future, and any such work stoppage&nbsp;could have a material adverse affect on the Company&#146;s business, financial condition and results of operations. There is no certainty that the current collective bargaining agreement will be extended or that a new collective bargaining agreement will be reached.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:28.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company sells ethanol to most of the major integrated oil companies, as well as a significant number of large, independent refiners and petroleum wholesalers.&#160; Trade receivables result primarily from ethanol marketing operations.&#160; As a general policy, collateral is not required for receivables, but customers&#146; financial condition and creditworthiness are evaluated regularly. Credit risk concentration related to accounts receivable resulted from the Company&#146;s top 10 customers having generated 65.6% and 61.7% of the consolidated net sales for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2011, Marathon Petroleum Corporation and Buckeye Energy Services, LLC (&#147;Buckeye&#148;) </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#147;ASU&#148;) 2011-05, <i>Presentation of Comprehensive Income</i> (&#147;ASU 2011-05&#148;), which changes the presentation requirements of comprehensive income to improve the comparability, consistency, and transparency of financial reporting and to increase the prominence of items reported in other comprehensive income.&#160; ASU 2011-05 requires that all non-owner changes in stockholders&#146; equity be presented either in a single continuous statement of comprehensive income or in two separate but consecutive statements. ASU 2011-05 is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2011.&#160; The Company does not anticipate that the adoption of ASU 2011-05 will have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-04, <i>Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (&#147;</i>IFRS<i>&#148;)</i> (&#147;ASU 2011-04&#148;), which changes certain fair value measurement and disclosure requirements, clarifies the application of existing fair value measurement and disclosure requirements and provides consistency to ensure that GAAP and IFRS fair value measurement and disclosure requirements are described in the same way.&#160; ASU 2011-04 is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2011.&#160; The Company does not anticipate that the adoption of ASU 2011-04 will have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">4.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Loss Per Share</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic loss&nbsp;per share excludes any dilution and is computed by dividing net loss attributable to common shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period. Diluted loss&nbsp;per share reflects the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock or resulted in the issuance of common stock that then shared in the earnings of the entity. The dilution from each of these instruments is calculated using the treasury stock method. Outstanding equity instruments that could potentially dilute basic loss per share in the future but were not included in the computation of diluted loss per share because they were antidilutive are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">5.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Measurements</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with ASC 820, the Company categorizes its investments and certain other assets and liabilities recorded at fair value into a three-level fair value hierarchy as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 1: Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 2: Quoted prices in markets that are not active, or inputs which are observable, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 3: Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (i.e., supported by little or no market activity).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Hierarchy on a Recurring Basis</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Available for sale securities</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s available for sale securities consists of shares of Imperial stock. The Company records the fair value of its Imperial stock using unadjusted quoted market prices, and accordingly, discloses these investments in Level&nbsp;1 of the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Realized gains (losses)</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recorded a net loss of $4.4 million on derivative transactions for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, and net gains of $0.6 million, $0.0 million and $1.2 million, respectively, for the ten months ended December&nbsp;31, 2010, the two months ended February&nbsp;28, 2010, and the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, in &#147;Gain (loss) on derivative transactions, net&#148; on the consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

The Notes outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2010, were redeemed on January&nbsp;21, 2011, at 105% of their carrying value.&#160; The fair value of the term loan and notes was determined based on Level 2 factors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">other-than-temporary.&#160; Such evaluation consists of a number of factors including, but not limited to, the length of time and extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, the financial condition and near term prospects of the issuer and management&#146;s ability and intent to hold the securities until fair value recovers.&#160; The assessment of the ability and intent to hold these securities to recovery focuses on liquidity needs, asset/liability management objectives and security portfolio objectives.&#160; Based on the results of the evaluation, management concluded that as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, the unrealized losses related to its 425,000 shares of Imperial were not temporary.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company previously held GPRE stock as available-for-sale securities.&#160; In October&nbsp;2010, the Company sold all of its GPRE securities for $4.2 million after commissions, resulting in a realized loss in the statement of operations for the ten months ended December&nbsp;31, 2010, of approximately $2.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Investments in Marketing Alliances</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had previously made non-controlling investments in other ethanol producers, which were recorded on the cost basis.&#160; All such investments were sold during 2009 with a recognized gain of $1.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">7.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s operations and cash flows are subject to fluctuations due to changes in commodity prices.&#160; As such, the Company has historically used various derivative financial instruments to minimize the effects of the volatility of commodity price changes primarily related to corn, natural gas, and ethanol.&#160; The Company monitors and manages its exposure as part of its overall risk management policy.&#160; As such, the Company seeks to reduce the potentially adverse effects that the volatility of these markets may have on its operating results. The Company may take derivative positions in these commodities as one way to mitigate risk.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to market risk with respect to the price and availability of corn, the principal raw material it uses to produce ethanol and ethanol by-products.&#160; In general, rising corn prices result in lower profit margins and, therefore, represent unfavorable market conditions.&#160; This is especially true when market conditions do not allow the Company to pass along increased corn costs to its customers.&#160; The availability and price of corn is subject to wide fluctuations due to unpredictable factors such as weather conditions, farmer planting decisions, governmental policies with respect to agriculture and international trade and global demand and supply.&#160; From time to time, the Company may have firm-price purchase commitments with some of its corn suppliers under which the Company agrees to buy corn at a price set in advance of the actual delivery of that corn.&#160; Under these arrangements, the Company assumes the risk of a price decrease in the market price of corn between the time this price is fixed and the time the corn is delivered.&#160; The Company accounts for these transactions as normal purchases under ASC 815, and accordingly, it does not mark these transactions to market.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company periodically enters into firm-price purchase commitments with some of its natural gas suppliers under which the Company agrees to buy natural gas at a price set in advance of the actual delivery of that natural gas.&#160; Under these arrangements, the Company assumes the risk of a price decrease in the market price of natural gas between the time this price is fixed and the time the natural gas is delivered.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company had purchased forward 527,000 MMBtu&#146;s of natural gas at an average fixed price of $3.28 per MMBtu through January&nbsp;2012.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2010, the Company had purchased forward 477,300 MMBtu&#146;s of natural gas at an average fixed price of $4.30 per MMBtu through the first quarter of 2011.&#160; The Company accounts for these transactions as normal purchases under ASC 815, and accordingly, it does not mark these transactions to market.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is also subject to market risk with respect to ethanol pricing.&#160; The Company&#146;s ethanol </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-26<a name="PB_26_103915_6228"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Construction-In-Progress</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2011, construction-in-progress includes $56.6 million related to the construction of the Aurora West plant, $23.0 million related to the Canton facility acquired in August&nbsp;2010, and $9.8 million related to capitalized projects at the Illinois facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2010, construction-in-progress includes $50.2 million related to the construction of the Aurora West plant, $67.0 million related to the construction of the Mt. Vernon plant and $17.1 million related to the Canton facility acquired in August&nbsp;2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">9.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Short-Term Borrowings</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had no short term borrowings at December&nbsp;31, 2011 or 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility with PNC Bank</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the Plan, on the Effective Date, the Company and its subsidiaries, as borrowers, entered into a Revolving Credit and Security Agreement (the &#147;Revolving Credit Agreement&#148;) with PNC Bank, National Association, as lender and as agent (&#147;PNC&#148;), providing for a $20&nbsp;million revolving credit facility (the &#147;Revolving Facility&#148;).&#160; On February&nbsp;28, 2011, the Company amended the Revolving Facility which increased the maximum loan amount to $30.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;20, 2011, the Revolving Credit Agreement with PNC was terminated and replaced with a revolving credit facility (the &#147;New Revolving Facility&#148;) with Wells Fargo Capital Finance, LLC.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revolving Credit Facility with Wells Fargo</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;20, 2011, the Company and each of its subsidiaries, as co-borrowers (collectively, the &#147;Borrowers&#148;), entered into the New Revolving Facility with the lenders party thereto (the &#147;Lenders&#148;), and Wells Fargo Capital Finance LLC as Lender and as agent for the Lenders (in such capacity, &#147;Wells Fargo&#148;) (as amended, and as may be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#147;New Revolving Facility Agreement&#148;) with a $50.0 million commitment (the &#147;Commitments&#148;).&#160; The New Revolving Facility has a borrowing base that is principally supported by accounts receivable and inventory.&#160; The Company terminated the Revolving Credit Agreement with PNC and paid a $0.6 million early termination fee.&#160; In addition, the Company expensed $39 thousand in related unamortized debt issuance costs.&#160; Both items are included in debt extinguishment costs for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; The Company capitalized $2.9 million in debt issuance costs for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, related to the New Revolving Facility Agreement. &#160;These costs will be amortized using the straight-line method over the term of the New Revolving Facility Agreement.&#160; The Company recognized $0.3 million of expense for the amortization of debt issuance costs related to the New Revolving Facility Agreement during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The loans under the New Revolving Facility will mature on the earlier of (a)&nbsp;July&nbsp;20, 2015, and (b)&nbsp;the date that is six (6) months before the maturity date of the indebtedness under the Term Loan Agreement (as defined below) (or if the indebtedness under the Term Loan Agreement is fully refinanced or replaced, the maturity date of such refinanced or replaced indebtedness).&#160; The New Revolving Facility has a borrowing base principally supported by the inventory and accounts receivable of the Borrowers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:28.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The rights and obligations of the lenders under the Revolving Credit Agreement have been assigned from PNC to Wells Fargo under the New Revolving Facility Agreement.&#160; The New Revolving Facility Agreement includes a grant of liens on substantially all of the assets of the Borrowers.&#160; The security interests granted under the New Revolving Facility in the assets (including inventory and accounts </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-28<a name="PB_28_103915_2639"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">receivable) other than substantially all of Borrowers&#146; fixed assets will be first priority in nature, subject to customary exceptions, and the security interests in the collateral constituting substantially all of the Borrowers&#146; fixed assets will be second priority in nature, and subject to customary liens and the first priority lien on such assets under Aventine&#146;s senior secured term loan credit agreement dated as of December&nbsp;22, 2010 by and among Aventine, as borrower, Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent and collateral agent (in such capacity, the &#147;Term Loan Agent&#148;), the lenders party thereto and certain other persons (as amended, and as may be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#147;Term Loan Agreement&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings under the New Revolving Facility Agreement will bear interest at (i)&nbsp;the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#147;LIBOR&#148;) plus 3.0% to 3.5% or (ii)&nbsp;the alternate base rate plus 2.0% to 2.5%.&#160; The applicable margin on loans under the New Revolving Facility will be re-determined on the first day of each fiscal quarter of Aventine by calculating the average amount that the Borrowers are entitled to borrow under the New Revolving Facility (after giving effect to any outstanding borrowings thereunder) as a proportion of the Commitments (as decreased by the amount of reductions in the Commitments pursuant to the New Revolving Facility).&#160; The alternate base rate will be calculated based on the greater of (A)&nbsp;the Federal funds rate plus 1/2 of 1.0%, (B)&nbsp;the LIBOR rate (calculated based upon an interest period of three months and determined on a daily basis), plus 1.0% and (C)&nbsp;the rate of interest announced, from time to time, by Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as its &#147;prime rate&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The New Revolving Facility Agreement requires mandatory prepayment of the obligations thereunder in the event that the amount of (i)&nbsp;outstanding revolving loans under the New Revolving Facility <i>plus</i> (ii)&nbsp;the aggregate undrawn amount of all outstanding letters of credit issued by certain Lenders exceeds the Borrowing Base (as defined in the New Revolving Facility Agreement).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The New Revolving Facility Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants concerning the conduct of Aventine&#146;s business operations, such as limitations on the incurrence of indebtedness, the granting of liens, maintenance of operations, mergers, consolidations and dispositions of assets, restricted payments and the payment of dividends, investments and transactions with affiliates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The New Revolving Facility Agreement contains a financial covenant that will require Aventine to maintain minimum liquidity levels of $25.0 million in 2013 and thereafter.&#160; The New Revolving Facility Agreement also includes customary events of default, including, but not limited to, failure to pay principal or interest, failure to pay or default under other material debt, misrepresentation or breach of warranty, violation of certain covenants, a change of control, the commencement of a bankruptcy proceeding, any of the Borrowers&#146; insolvency and the rendering of a judgment or judgments against any of the Borrowers&#146; in excess of a specified amount individually or in the aggregate.&#160; Upon the occurrence of an event of default, Aventine&#146;s obligations under the New Revolving Facility Agreement may be accelerated and all indebtedness thereunder would become immediately due and payable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company had no short term borrowings and letters of credit outstanding of $9.2 million, respectively, under the New Revolving Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Senior Secured Term Loan Credit Agreement</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;22, 2010, the Company entered into the Term Loan Agreement with the Term Loan Agent, the lenders party thereto, Citigroup Global Markets Inc. and Jefferies Finance LLC, as joint lead arrangers and joint book-runners, and Citibank, N.A. and Jefferies Finance LLC, as co-syndication agents. Under the Term Loan Agreement, the lenders provided to the Company an aggregate principal amount $200 million term loan facility (the &#147;Term Loan Facility&#148;).&#160; The Term Loan Facility was issued net of original issue discount of $8.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Also on December&nbsp;22, 2010, the Company gave notice of redemption pursuant to the indenture dated as of the Effective Date among the Company, each of the Company&#146;s direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries, as guarantors, and Wilmington Trust FSB, as trustee and collateral agent, providing that it would redeem all $155.0 million aggregate principal amount of Notes at a redemption price of 105% of the principal amount thereof, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but not including, the redemption date. Concurrently with the closing of the Term Loan Agreement, the Company irrevocably deposited in trust with the trustee for the Notes, $164.8 million of the proceeds from the Term Loan Facility, funds sufficient to pay the redemption price for all $155.0 million aggregate principal amount of the Notes. Accordingly, the Notes and the restricted cash for payment of the Notes were included in current liabilities and current assets, respectively, in the condensed consolidated balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2010. The Company redeemed such Notes on January&nbsp;21, 2011.&#160; In connection with the redemption, the Company paid $164.8 million, of which $155.0 million related to the principal amount of the Notes, $7.8 million related to a prepayment penalty on the Notes and $2.0 million related to interest on the Notes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;7, 2011, the Company entered into an incremental amendment (the &#147;Incremental Amendment&#148;) with the Term Loan Agent and Macquarie Bank Limited, as lender (&#147;Macquarie&#148;), to the</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-30<a name="PB_30_103915_8299"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Company&#146;s Term Loan Agreement.&nbsp; Pursuant to the Incremental Amendment, Macquarie loaned an aggregate principal amount equal to $25.0 million, before fees of $1.3 million in fees, to the Company.&nbsp; The loan under the Incremental Amendment has substantially the same terms as the existing loans under the Term Loan Agreement, including seniority, ranking in right of payment and of security, maturity date, applicable margin and interest rate floor.&nbsp; The Company continues to be subject to all other terms and restrictions contained in the original Term Loan Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings under the Term Loan Agreement bear interest at (i)&nbsp;LIBOR plus 8.5% per annum or (ii)&nbsp;the alternate base rate plus 7.5% per annum. &#160;The LIBOR rate is subject to a 2% floor.&nbsp; The alternate base rate will be calculated based on the greater of (i)&nbsp;3% per annum and (ii)&nbsp;the highest of (A)&nbsp;the Federal funds rate plus 1/2 of 1%, (B)&nbsp;the LIBOR rate for an interest period of one month plus 1%, (C)&nbsp;the three-month certificate of deposit rate plus 1/2 of 1%, and (D)&nbsp;Citibank, N.A.&#146;s prime rate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;20, 2011, the Company entered into an amendment (&#147;Citi Amendment&#148;) to the Term Loan Agreement with the lenders party thereto and the Term Loan Agent.&#160; Under the terms of the Citi Amendment, the amount of indebtedness that the Company is permitted to incur under the New Revolving Facility (including bank products and hedging obligations) is capped at $58.0 million. The Citi Amendment reduces the Company&#146;s minimum liquidity covenant for 2012 from $25.0 million to $15.0 million. The Citi Amendment also includes certain technical amendments to permit the New Revolving Facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, and the ten months ended December&nbsp;31, 2010, the Company recorded $2.1 and $3.6 million, respectively, of capitalized interest related to its capacity expansion project in Aurora, Nebraska, and $0.7 and $2.6 million, respectively, of capitalized interest related to its capacity expansion projects in Mt. Vernon,&nbsp;Indiana and $1.4 and $0.0 million of capitalized interest related to its capacity expansion in Canton,&nbsp;Illinois.&#160; The Company did not capitalize any interest for the two months ended February&nbsp;28, 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">13.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Lease Commitments</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases certain assets such as rail cars, terminal facilities, barges, buildings and equipment from unaffiliated parties under non-cancelable operating leases.&#160; Terms of the leases, including renewals, vary by lease. Rental expense for operating leases for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, the ten months ended December&nbsp;31, 2010, the two months ended February&nbsp;28, 2010, and the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, was $6.8 million, $3.6 million, $0.6 million,&#160; and $9.2 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had capital lease obligations of $0.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011, which were payable through 2013 at an assumed interest rate of 8.0%.&#160; Such capital leases are recorded in &#147;Other long-term liabilities&#148; on the consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
